15 An old-fashioned 60 W lamp converts 95% of its energy supply into heat. A 4.0 W modern lamp
has the same power output of light as the old-fashioned lamp.
What is the efficiency of the modern lamp?
A
5.0%
B
6.7%
C
75%
D
95%

hints: Notice the $60\text{ W}$ is total input power and $95\%$ of it is wasted heat, so work out what power is left for useful light.
Recall efficiency is $\text{useful power output} / \text{total power input}$, and both lamps have the same useful light power.
Calculate the old lamp light power first, then divide that same $\text{W}$ value by the modern lamp $4.0\text{ W}$ input and multiply by $100\%$.
walkthrough: Useful output for a lamp is light power. For the old lamp, input power $P_{in} = 60\text{ W}$ and $95\%$ becomes heat.
So the fraction becoming light is $1 - 0.95 = 0.05$. Light power $P_{light} = 0.05 \times 60\text{ W} = 3.0\text{ W}$.
The modern lamp produces the same light power, so its useful output is also $P_{useful} = 3.0\text{ W}$, while its input is $P_{in} = 4.0\text{ W}$.
As a percentage this is $0.75 \times 100\% = 75\%$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is the efficiency of the old $60\text{ W}$ lamp, since $100\% - 95\% = 5\%$ goes to light, not the efficiency of the $4.0\text{ W}$ lamp.

B.explanation: This is the ratio of input powers $4.0/60$, which does not give useful light power divided by input power for the modern lamp.

C.explanation: Useful light power is $3.0\text{ W}$ and input is $4.0\text{ W}$, so efficiency is $3.0/4.0 = 0.75 = 75\%$.

D.explanation: This is the fraction of the old lamp input wasted as heat, not the fraction of the modern lamp input converted to useful light.
